newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Almaz silent on platinum export resumption.
newsitem.headline: Russian Almaz silent on platinum export resumption.

text.p: Russia's Almazjuvelirexport, the state metals export agency, declined on Wednesday to comment on whether it had resumed platinum exports to Japan.
Representatives of the agency said senior officials Vitaly Berlin and Sergei Gorny were on a business trip until Monday, while Andrei Travkin declined to speak to reporters.
Gorny told Reuters on July 15 deliveries of both platinum group metals had resumed July 8. He and other officials have declined to comment on the matter since then.
Traders in Japan say Moscow resumed exports of palladium earlier this month but that platinum deliveries had not yet been sighted.
Russia is the world's largest supplier of palladium and second largest of platinum, with Japan the leading consumer of both white metals.

Moscow delayed shipments of the metals for around seven months, fuelling price hikes for the metals and market talk that Russians supplies could be dwindling. Throughout the matter, Almazjuvelirexport gave various dates for the resumption of supplies and reasons for the delays. --Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
